title: Customer need scouting compass + microproposals
content:
Goal: quick, operationally-actionable map from recent customer interviews (Dec 2026–Jan 2027) to small experiments and short-implementation feature proposals. This doc is intentionally lightweight — capture patterns, concrete asks, hypothesis-backed impact estimates, and the smallest possible probes we can run in 2–6 weeks.

Context + observed patterns (raw):
- Multiple mid-market customers report two related pain points: unpredictable per-request cost spikes and hard-to-explain latency regressions during traffic bursts. They want better signal to triage and lighter knobs to reduce cost without manual model swaps.
- Platform teams want deterministic fallback behavior when dedicated pools degrade. They prefer automated, auditable fallbacks rather than ad-hoc engineering overrides.
- A few AI-native startups asked for a tiny control plane API: per-route KV-cache invalidation and short-lived override TTLs for cache entries during experiments.
- Several customers building chat assistants cited difficulty debugging hallucination regressions after model rollouts; they requested prompt-set based quality monitors that trigger fast rollbacks.
- One regulated customer asked for a minimal proof-of-concept: audit trail linking tokens generated to the model version + rollout tag for a 30-day window.

Representative raw quotes (anonymized):
- "Our token bill jumps randomly when a few users run long sessions — we need a quick way to cap cost per-session without breaking UX."
- "Fallback logic currently feels manual; when capacity throttles we still get 500s and noisy errors. We want predictable fallthroughs."

Patterns -> microproposals (ordered by implementation effort, short description, why it helps):
1) Per-session token budget enforcement (effort: small)
   - What: a per-session token cap that cuts generation and returns a structured partial output + reason code when hit. Expose via SDK config and request header.
   - Why: immediate stopgap to prevent runaway bills; customers can add UX fallback (summaries, ask to continue) rather than seeing huge token spikes.
   - Suggested probe: roll out to 3 beta teams, default cap 2048 tokens for long-running chat flows; measure aborted completions, user-continue rates, and cost reduction.

2) Prefix/KV cache invalidation API (effort: small–medium)
   - What: an endpoint to invalidate specific prefixes or cache keys, and a short-lived override TTL for experiments.
   - Why: enables rapid iteration on prompt templates and immediate quality fixes without model restarts or global cache clears.
   - Probe: give two customers early access for 2 weeks; track number of invalidations, mean time to mitigation for regressions.

3) Deterministic fallback policy builder (effort: medium)
   - What: UI + config DSL to compose fallback chains (region -> model-variant -> queued-mode). Includes audit log entries when a fallback was triggered and reason code.
   - Why: reduces manual incident triage, gives customers predictable behavior during capacity events.
   - Probe: create a canned policy template for Dedicated customers; simulate degraded capacity in staging and verify deterministic route.

4) Prompt-set quality monitors + rollback hooks (effort: medium–large)
   - What: allow customers to upload small prompt sets with expected outputs/metrics (BLEU, exact-match, hallucination flags). Monitor live drift and wire an automated canary rollback trigger with human approval.
   - Why: prevents silent quality regressions after rollouts.
   - Probe: pilot with one enterprise customer that experiences rollouts monthly; aim for detection->alert in <6 hours.

5) Token-level attribution in audit trail (effort: medium)
   - What: store minimal mapping metadata that links generation token ranges to model version & rollout tag. Queryable for 30 days. Expose as CSV export for compliance customers.
   - Why: regulatory ask + debugging utility for customer success and security reviews.
   - Probe: implement sample export for a single customer for 30 days and validate legal team's checklist.

Fast wins (can be shipped within 1–3 sprints):
- Per-session token cap (1 sprint)
- Cache invalidation API (small slice: invalidate-by-prefix) (2 sprints)
- Admin-only UI toggle for deterministic fallback templates (1 sprint)

Impact scoring rubric (simple):
- Customer pain frequency (1–3) + business impact (1–3) + implement risk (1–3, inverted) => total. Use to prioritize pilots.
- Example scoring: per-session cap = 3 (freq) + 3 (impact) + 2 (low risk => score 2) = 8/9.

Open questions & unknowns (for engineering/product):
- Storage/compute cost: token-level attribution requires retention — minimal metadata only? do we store offsets vs full tokens? (engineering input needed).
- UX: how should SDKs surface per-session caps? Throw an error, return a structured status, or stream a special event? Need client SDK owners.
- Telemetry: what telemetry labels unlock fast triage for fallback occurrences (route, pool, model-variant, customer-tier)? Propose baseline labels and get SRE sign-off.

Suggested next steps (owner and timeline):
- Week 1: Product + SRE sync to scope telemetry labels and create JIRA epic for per-session-caps (owner: Jon Ruiz).
- Week 2: Deliver cache-invalidation API design doc and create two pilot JIRA issues for engineering (owner: Maya Sokolov).
- Week 3: Identify one enterprise customer for prompt-set monitor pilot; legal/PS to review audit scope (owner: Aisha Patel).

Risk flags and mitigation notes:
- Automated rollback hooks could cause outsized churn if thresholds are too aggressive — require human gating for first 3 months.
- Cache invalidation could be misused to create operational load (many invalidations). Add rate-limits and admin audit trail.

Appendix: short customer vignettes (for context)
- Vignette A (SaaS analytics startup): heavy conversational sessions (avg 12 messages), occasional admin reports hitting 30k tokens/session after long threads. Willing to adopt per-session cap if SDK surfaces graceful continue flow.
- Vignette B (Retail chatbot): uses dedicated pool; when capacity throttles, users see 502s. They want fallback chain that serves smaller LMs rather than errors.

Notes to self: share this doc with eng-hosted-api and eng-serve-runtime on Monday. Create a short feedback form for pilot customers asking: perceived reduction in surprise costs, ease of use, and any new friction introduced.

Unresolved: naming — do we call the SDK knob "session_token_budget" or "max_tokens_per_conversation"? Quick poll in #eng-sdk tomorrow.

End of doc.
